This Criminal Miscellaneous case is filed to quash the proceedings in CC No. 389/2016 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Kanjirappally arising from Crime No. 969/2015 of Ponkunnam Police Ststion.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Kanjirappally
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged are under Secs.323, 354, 498A, 420 r/w 34 IPC.

According to the petitioners, even if the entire allegations are accepted, there is absolutely no ingredients to attract Sec.498A IPC as far as the petitioners are concerned, who are the 1st accused and 2nd accused in this case.
It is also contended by the petitioners that all the alleged incident even as per Annexure-A complaint happened at Bangalore.

The counsel also submitted that an 2024:KER:75166 order passed under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is set aside, for the reason that the court has no jurisdiction to entertain the same.

sentences.text: After hearing both sides, I am of the considered opinion that the petitioners can be allowed to file a discharge petition before the trial court in absentia.

If such a discharge petition is filed within a time frame, the learned Magistrate will consider all the contentions raised by the petitioners before this Court and till final orders are passed in the discharge petition, the presence of the petitioners shall not be insisted.

Therefore, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is 2024:KER:75166 disposed of in the following manner:
1. The petitioners are free to file a discharge petition before the jurisdictional court within thirty days from the date of receipt of a stamped certified copy of this order, if charge is not framed.

2. Once such a discharge petition is received, the jurisdictional court will consider the same and pass appropriate orders in it, after giving an opportunity of hearing to the petitioners and the Prosecutor concerned, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate,
within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the discharge petition.
3. If a discharge petition is filed as directed above, the presence of the petitioners shall not be insisted, till final orders are passed in the discharge petition.
All the contentions raised by the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous case are left open and the petitioners are free to agitate the same in the discharge petition.
